description: The image displays three pie charts labeled “easy,” “medium,” and “hard,” each illustrating the distribution of four categories—N+K+, N−K+, N−K−, and N+K−—across different difficulty levels of a task, likely related to geometric knowledge reasoning with large language models as suggested by the paper title. The legend on the right identifies N+K+ as teal, N−K+ as light yellow, N−K− as orange, and N+K− as reddish-orange. In the “easy” chart, N+K+ dominates at 55.4%, followed by N−K+ at 38.3%, N−K− at 4.6%, and N+K− at 1.7%. The “medium” chart shows a similar pattern: N+K+ at 58.8%, N−K+ at 35.4%, N−K− at 4.0%, and N+K− at 1.8%. In the “hard” chart, the distribution shifts: N−K− and N−K+ are nearly equal at 37.9% and 37.3% respectively, while N+K+ drops to 18.1% and N+K− remains low at 6.7%. Each slice is labeled with its percentage, and the charts are visually aligned for comparison, with no exploded slices or additional annotations beyond the percentages and legend.
